matchups.recap: Arben got absolutely buttfucked by 17.7 points this week, and honestly, that's being generous to whatever dumpster fire he called a lineup. 113.6 points is what you score when you're either injured, asleep, or—let's be real—both. Rob walked into this matchup like he was carrying a loaded gun and Arben showed up with a fucking pool noodle, getting outscored by nearly two full players' worth of points because apparently his roster has all the production of a practice squad on bye week.

Flamur got absolutely skull-fucked by an 18.5 point margin this week, and honestly, that feels generous—dude's team played like it was on a 6-week vacation. 112.4 points is what you score when your "studs" decide to take turns being completely useless, and apparently Flamur's entire roster got that memo simultaneously. Nori didn't even need to bring his A-game to demolish this disaster; he just showed up and watched Flamur's season spiral down the drain like a turd that won't flush. Better luck next week, chief—you're gonna need it.

Ben got absolutely obliterated by 69.3 points—which is funny because that's also how many brain cells he's got left after whatever the fuck that roster construction was. Watching his team collapse like a house of cards built by a drunk toddler while Rinor put up 148 must've felt like getting kicked in the nuts by a horse wearing steel-toed boots. Ben didn't just lose this week, he got publicly executed on the scoreboard, and honestly, 78.7 points is what you deserve when you make lineup decisions based on vibes and ESPN's injury report from 2019.

Veton got absolutely skull-fucked by 3 points this week—so close he could taste it, yet so far he had to watch Adam's mid-tier roster shuffle-step into the end zone. This is what happens when you play fantasy like you're making decisions with your eyes closed and your brain tied behind your back: you lose by the kind of margin that'll haunt you at family dinners for the next six months. Better luck next week, chief—you're gonna need it.

Rilind got absolutely buttfucked by a 25-point margin this week, and honestly, it's not even surprising at this point—his roster management is so dogshit he probably thought he was playing in a different league. Faton waltzed into the end zone while Rilind's lineup sat there like a bunch of parking lot attendants watching the game from the sidelines. At this rate, Rilind's team is held together with duct tape and prayers, and apparently both just ran out.

Ilir just got absolutely cock-blocked by his own family by 1.3 points—that's the fantasy football equivalent of losing Thanksgiving dinner bragging rights to a relative you can't even avoid at Christmas. Peter's gonna be milking this at every family gathering for the next year, and Ilir's gotta sit there knowing he left points on the bench like a fucking amateur. That's not just a loss, that's a family L that's gonna sting every time someone passes the potatoes.

matchups.preview: Rob's already halfway to the lottery with that 1-4 record, and now he's gotta face the one team in this league that actually knows what they're doing—Nori's sitting pretty at 4-1 while Rob's been out here making decisions like he's playing with his eyes closed. This is gonna be a bloodbath, and Rob's going home wondering why he even bothered setting his lineup.

Ben's already halfway to a losing record and it's not even halfway through the season—this week he's about to get exposed by a guy who actually knows how to build a roster. Arben's been running circles around this league while Ben's out here playing checkers with his waiver wire pickups, and this matchup is gonna feel like a fucking execution.

Veton's rolling into this week like a man who thought "sure, let's start three guys on bye week" was a legitimate strategy—0-5 and somehow still finding new ways to lose. Flamur's sitting pretty at 4-1, which means he's about to get absolutely humbled by the one team in this league that's been actively trying to tank harder than a full-size SUV in the Atlantic. This is the matchup where 0-5 finally gets a win, and Flamur's gonna spend all of next week explaining how he "totally would've won" if literally any of his studs had shown up on Sunday.

Both of you are limping along at .500 like a couple of middle-aged guys trying to stay relevant, but here's the thing—one of you is about to get exposed this week, and honestly it could go either way since you're both equally mediocre right now. Faton's barely holding on by the skin of his teeth while Rinor's probably convinced himself he's still got it, so whoever chokes harder on Sunday loses the right to talk shit at the bar for the next week. May the least incompetent team win, you frauds.

Ilir's sitting pretty at 3-2 thinking he's got this thing figured out, but we all know that's just the eye of the hurricane before he inevitably implodes like he does every goddamn year. Adam's been treading water at 2-3, which means he's either about to get hot at exactly the wrong time or continue being the league's most consistent disappointment—either way, this matchup is a coin flip between two teams with no business being this close to .500.

Jetmir's sitting pretty at 3-2 while Rilind's dumpster fire is burning at 1-4, which means this should be a bloodbath—except Jetmir's probably about to choke it away like he does every time he gets comfortable, and Rilind's got nothing to lose, which somehow makes him more dangerous than a guy who actually knows what he's doing.
